summary: This work demonstrates error semi-transparent (EsT) universal control of a bosonic logical qubit using linear drives on a binomial 'kitten' code in a superconducting cavity coupled to a transmon ancilla. EsT operations leverage dynamic encoding subspaces to achieve fault-tolerant gates with reduced infidelity conditioned on photon loss, extending active-manipulation lifetimes under quantum error correction.
motivation: While bosonic codes have demonstrated beyond-break-even quantum memory, realizing fault-tolerant logical operations remains a bottleneck for scaled quantum computation. Prior error-transparent gate demonstrations were limited to phase gates, and theoretical proposals for amplitude-mixing gates required strong nonlinear drives impractical for oscillator control.
method: The authors develop a framework based on dynamic (time-evolving) code and error subspaces that enables simple linear cavity and qubit drives to achieve universal EsT gates. Drive amplitudes $\epsilon(t)$ and $\Omega(t)$ are numerically optimized using GRAPE with a weighted cost function combining code-space fidelity, error-transparency metrics (QEC violation, leakage, trajectory mismatch), and velocity variance. Gates are implemented with 1 µs (X, H) and 0.6 µs (T) durations on a cavity with $T_1 = 180$ µs and ancilla with $T_1 = 70$ µs.
result: EsT gates achieve a five-fold reduction in infidelity conditioned on photon loss ($F_{\mathrm{err|jump}}$ increases from 0.45 to 0.85 for X gate), 17-fold reduction in error-space operation infidelity ($F_{\mathrm{err}}$ from 0.4 to 0.95), and improved performance after single autonomous QEC correction steps. An eight-gate composite non-Clifford sequence ($THXTHTХX$) preserves EsT properties with 3.6× infidelity reduction in error space.
